title: Mini ablation gauge + run scoreboard
content:
Purpose: super-compact personal ledger for quick ablation runs — capture p50/p95, cost ballpark, and one-line takeaways so I can decide follow-ups without re-running long dashboards.

Hypothesis: small kv-cache + 4-bit quantization retains >95% quality on short prompts (<128 tokens) while cutting cost ~2.5x and improving p50 by ~20%. Need to sanity-check throughput side-effects for bursty traffic.

Quick run table (columns: run, date, model, quant, kv_cache, batch, seq_len, tokens, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, quality_notes)
A01 | 2025-11-22 | llama2-13b | fp16 | none | 1 | 64 | 120 | 78 | 210 | 1.00 | baseline prompts (10) -> baseline quality
A02 | 2025-11-22 | llama2-13b | int4 | none | 1 | 64 | 118 | 62 | 180 | 0.42 | int4 faster, slight tokenization oddities on punctuation
A03 | 2025-11-23 | llama2-13b | int4 | prefix-cache (32k) | 1 | 64 | 118 | 55 | 170 | 0.38 | cache wins p95 on repeated prefixes
A04 | 2025-11-24 | llama2-13b | int4 | prefix-cache (32k) | 8 | 64 | 910 | 420 | 980 | 0.12 | batching improves cost but p50 per-request worse as expected; throughput x7 observed
A05 | 2025-12-02 | mixformer-7b | int8 | kv-cache (8k) | 1 | 128 | 210 | 130 | 350 | 0.26 | 7b pretty good latency; quality similar to 13b on short prompts
A06 | 2025-12-14 | mixformer-7b | int8 | kv-cache (8k) | 4 | 128 | 820 | 480 | 1100 | 0.09 | high throughput, watch tail latency for MLP-heavy prompts
A07 | 2026-01-10 | llama2-13b | q4_k | kv-cache (32k) | 1 | 64 | 116 | 58 | 160 | 0.35 | q4_k slightly tighter than int4 on cost; quality check pass on quick eval
A08 | 2026-01-25 | llama2-13b | q4_k | kv-cache (32k) | 2 | 64 | 230 | 120 | 380 | 0.19 | 2-concurrency: p50 doubles, but cost per-1k improves with packing

Observations / notes to self:
- Cache configuration matters more than quant on tail (p95) when prefix repetition high.
- Batching gives great cost-per-1k but increases p50 for single-call services — think about route-level policy: dedicated low-batch lanes for interactive flows.
- mixformer-7b is a good candidate for background tasks where cost matters and prompts are slightly longer.
- Need a small A/B eval across 200 real user prompts to confirm perceived quality delta for q4_k vs int4.

Next steps (short):
- [ ] Create a 200-prompt quick-eval set from production prompt-sample (ask SRE for anonymized sample) — target by 2026-02-12.
- [ ] Run q4_k vs int4 on the 200-set, capture exact semantic similarity and BLEU-ish metric, push results to gist.
- [ ] File infra ticket for route:interactive-low-batch (ties to JIRA-7892).

Open questions / TODOs (notes style):
- How much mem overhead does prefix-cache 32k add on a single 16GB GPU? quick check on infra node.
- When using batching=8 we saw x7 throughput; does that hold at larger seq_len (512)? schedule a short ramp test.
- Check whether kernel selection in runtime picks faster GEMM for q4_k by default; if not, add flag to force.

Scratch formulas (for mental arithmetic during quick checks):
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd = (instance_hour_cost_usd / tokens_per_hour) * 1000  // rough derivation used here
- tokens_per_hour approx = (3600 / p50_ms) * avg_tokens_per_request * concurrency_efficiency_factor

Quick links & references used:
- infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 (batch scheduling fixes)
- convo: slack:#runtime-bench (thread: "mini-ablation q4_k vs int4")

Format notes: this is my pared-down tracker for decisions. Keep concise — move polished results to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/bench-reports once I have full eval.

-- Odette (quick log)
